_meta.indication: OSPHENA is an estrogen agonist/antagonist indicated for the treatment of moderate to severe dyspareunia, a symptom of vulvar and vaginal atrophy, due to menopause

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.population: Generally healthy postmenopausal women (826 enrolled) aged 41 to 81 with vulvar and vaginal atrophy due to menopause
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Mean change from baseline to week 12 in the moderate to severe symptom self-identified by the patient as most bothersome (dyspareunia)
pivotal_trials.n: N=110 OSPHENA 60 mg, N=113 placebo (dyspareunia mITT population)
pivotal_trials.result: LS mean change in dyspareunia severity at Week 12: -1.39 for OSPHENA 60 mg vs -0.89 placebo; p=0.0012

nct_ctgov.title: A Clinical Study to Evaluate Ospemifene in the Treatment of Vulvar and Vaginal Atrophy in Postmenopausal Women

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.population: Generally healthy postmenopausal women (919 enrolled) aged 41 to 79 with moderate to severe vaginal dryness or dyspareunia cohort
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Mean change from baseline to week 12 in the moderate to severe most bothersome symptom (dyspareunia)
pivotal_trials.n: N=301 OSPHENA 60 mg, N=297 placebo (dyspareunia mITT population)
pivotal_trials.result: LS mean change in dyspareunia severity at Week 12: -1.55 for OSPHENA 60 mg vs -1.29 placebo; p<0.0001

nct_ctgov.title: Efficacy and Safety of Ospemifene in the Treatment of Moderate to Severe Vaginal Dryness and Vaginal Pain Associated With Sexual Activity

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=1%): hot flush (7.5% vs 2.6% placebo), vaginal discharge (3.8% vs 0.3%), muscle spasms (3.2% vs 0.9%), genital discharge (1.3% vs 0.1%), hyperhidrosis (1.6% vs 0.6%). Serious identified risks include venous and arterial thrombotic events and endometrial effects.
target_moa: Ospemifene is an estrogen agonist/antagonist that binds to human estrogen receptors (ERalpha and ERbeta) and causes estrogen-like effects on the vaginal epithelium
modality: Small molecule (estrogen agonist/antagonist, formerly termed a SERM)

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: ENDOMETRIAL CANCER AND CARDIOVASCULAR DISORDERS — increased risk of endometrial cancer with unopposed estrogen agonism on the endometrium, and increased risk of stroke and deep vein thrombosis (DVT)

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because outside expertise was not necessary and there were no controversial issues

description.text: Added new indication for treatment of moderate to severe vaginal dryness, a symptom of vulvar and vaginal atrophy, due to menopause

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for a new indication for the treatment of moderate to severe vaginal dryness, a symptom of vulvar and vaginal atrophy, due to menopause.

summary.text: Standard NDA for a new molecular entity (estrogen agonist/antagonist) approved on full approval based on two randomized placebo-controlled Phase 3 trials showing improvement in dyspareunia; no advisory committee was convened and no accelerated approval or special designation was applied.

citations.quote: Shionogi, Inc. submitted an NDA (203-505) for a new molecular entity (NME) containing an estrogen agonist/antagonist in a tablet formulation designated as ospemifene (tradename Osphena). Each ospemifene tablet contains 60 mg of the active ingredient to be taken once daily orally with food.
